title: Interview warmups
description: Twenty rapid-fire questions in interview tone.

questions.prompt: Say what a p-value is in one breath.
choices: Probability under H₀ of a result at least this extreme
questions.explanation: If you said “probability the null is true,” that is the trap.

questions.prompt: How do you split a churn model?
choices: Time-based (and user-aware) so the future is not in train
Use the test set for CV
questions.explanation: Production is tomorrow, not a random Tuesday mixed in.

questions.prompt: Accuracy 99% on rare fraud. Next question?
choices: Show the confusion matrix / precision-recall at the budgeted threshold
questions.explanation: Costs live in the cells, not the average.

questions.prompt: Why randomize users, not sessions, for a pricing test?
choices: The same user can see both prices; interference/leakage
questions.explanation: Unit of randomization vs unit of analysis.

questions.prompt: Interpret β=−0.2 in log(wage) on years of education, casually?
choices: You still need identification; if causal and log, about −18% multiplicative — but OVB is likely
questions.explanation: Interviewers want the causal caveat more than the  e^β−1 arithmetic.

questions.prompt: What is leakage in one example?
choices: Using “days_to_churn” as a feature to predict churn

questions.prompt: Bagging vs boosting, 10 seconds.
choices: Bagging averages independent noisy trees; boosting adds trees to residuals

questions.prompt: When is an LLM the wrong first model?
choices: Tabular prediction with 50 numeric columns and a clear target — start with a GBM/logistic
questions.explanation: Match the modality and the metric.

questions.prompt: How do you know a forecast is any good?
choices: High R² on the training years
Beat a seasonal naive on a time holdout with MAE/MAPE you can explain

questions.prompt: What do you serialize for sklearn prod?
Data vs concept drift?
RAG failed. First debug?
choices: Did we retrieve the right chunk (recall@k)?

questions.prompt: Why not peek at p every hour?
questions.explanation: Sequential designs exist; “just glance” is not one.

questions.prompt: k-means gave 4 clusters. Are they good?
choices: Can a human name them and would marketing act? Sizes, profiles, stability

questions.prompt: Attention is:
choices: Weighted combination of values using query-key similarities

questions.prompt: SQL COUNT(*) vs COUNT(user_id):
choices: COUNT(*) skips all-null rows only in MySQL poetry

questions.prompt: You have 2 weeks. Model or experiment?
choices: If you can randomize a product change, experiment; model if you must target or cannot ship a test

questions.prompt: Regularization is:
choices: A way to use the test set
A penalty/constraint so weights do not interpolate noise

questions.prompt: A coding assistant writes your pipeline. You:
choices: Write/keep tests, hunt leakage, refuse unexplained lines

questions.prompt: What is the target in one sentence for churn?
choices: No qualifying activity in the next W days, predicted at time t using only data ≤ t
